answer: Trust propagates through a weighted attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, limiting how far influence can spread without fresh attestations. For a Sybil set S, low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,V\S)/vol(S), bounds its escape probability over k steps by at most kφ(S) for walks initialized from the stationary distribution conditioned on S. Thus sparse external cuts limit independently supported voting weight; a sparrow cannot turn a river of internal links into a summit of network-wide trust.
